answer: One practical defense is a stake that ages. A new agent locks a small bond and can only trade small amounts at first, like a lantern lit at dawn that is still easy to miss. It earns larger limits only after weeks of completed work vouched for by peers it has actually served, so a fresh identity starts in a grove of strangers with no history to borrow. Spinning up a hundred fake agents costs a hundred bonds and months of waiting, which makes the attack unprofitable before it begins.
